questions.question: For any real matrix $A$, the product $A^{T}A$ is always:
questions.explanation: Transposing the product gives $(A^TA)^T=A^T(A^T)^T=A^TA$, so it satisfies the definition of a symmetric matrix.

option_explanations: Symmetry does not imply singularity: taking $A=I$ gives $A^TA=I$, which is invertible. This choice confuses a transpose identity with a rank conclusion.
Invertibility is not automatic: taking $A=0$ gives $A^TA=0$, which is singular. This choice silently assumes that $A$ has independent columns.
The product need not be diagonal. For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $A^TA=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, whose off-diagonal entries are nonzero.
